items.summaryZh: 20岁的安德烈亚·安东内利正在让F1车阵看起来像一群迟钝的退休者。但显然，在梅赛德斯驾驶2026年世界锦标赛并不足以让这位意大利天才感到满足。

media.altZh: 安东内利透露计划在F1外开设自己的赛车学院 · 第 1 张

items.originalTitle: Kimi Antonelli reveals plans to launch his own racing academy outside F1
detailZh: 基米·安东内利透露计划在F1之外开设自己的赛车学院
F1明星基米·安东内利告诉AMUS，他想要开设自己的车手学院，并与他的父亲在GT3赛车中搭档
对于梅赛德斯粉丝来说，这里是关于银箭的最新消息，包括来自布拉克利和布里克斯沃斯的F1新闻、车手更新、赛车发展和比赛分析
年仅20岁的安德烈亚·基米·安东内利目前正在忙于让其他F1车手看起来像一群迟钝的退休者。但显然，在梅赛德斯赛车中轻松统治2026年世界锦标赛并不能完全让这位意大利天才满足。
在最近的一次与德国《Auto Motor und Sport》的访谈中，安东内利透露，他已经计划在F1围场之外进行他的下一个重大举措：建立自己的车手学院。
随着最近围场内关于兰多·诺里斯成立自己的青训车队的讨论，安东内利也想分得驾驶人才培养这块蛋糕。鉴于他从小就成长在他父亲GT赛车队的车库中，AKM Motorsport，他深知对于一个有才华但没有金钱的孩子来说，财务阶梯是多么残酷。
“我们想为年轻人建立一个学院，让他们有机会进入赛车运动，”安东内利告诉AMUS。“赛车运动是一个伟大但艰难的世界。在那里获得机会并不容易。我们想帮助年轻车手获得机会。”
有趣的是，安东内利并没有将他的未来学院严格定位在将孩子们引入一级方程式培养系列。他明确指出，专业GT赛车是一条高度可行、利润丰厚的道路——这种想法在很大程度上受到了某位三次世界冠军的影响。
马克斯·维斯塔潘几乎将GT3耐力赛世界变成了他个人的副任务，而F1车阵中的其他人则集体患上了恐惧错失综合症。安东内利也不例外。
安德烈亚·基米·安东内利，梅赛德斯，马克斯·维斯塔潘，红牛车队
"GT赛车目前正处于强劲的增长势头，"安东内利在接受AMUS采访时确认。"马克斯正在帮助它变得更加知名，并展示出它的魅力。"
考虑到这种蓬勃的增长势头，安东内利希望他未来的学院能够为年轻车手们撒下更广泛的网。"这并不一定非要是一级方程式，"他补充道。"在专业GT赛车领域也有很多机会。"
在安东内利开始为一家完整的青训车队签支票之前，他还有一件更加私人的赛车运动生意要处理。
他的父亲，马可·安东内利，是一位前房车赛车手，他建立了非常成功的AKM赛车运动公司。虽然基米之前测试过他父亲的GT3赛车，但两人从未在一场现场赛车周末中共同驾驶过赛车。根据基米的说法，这种情况很快就要改变了。
马可·安东内利，安德烈亚·基米·安东内利的父亲，梅赛德斯
"我们几乎分享了一切，尤其是在赛车运动方面。我们还有未来的共同项目，"安东内利解释道。"我父亲的梦想是有一天我们能一起比赛。三年前，我为他的车队参赛，但我们从未作为队友一起参加过比赛。我们希望在GT3赛车中实现这一点。"
当AMUS询问关于这个备受期待的父子组合的时间表时，安东内利毫不犹豫地将它排进了日程。
"如果我们有时间，绝对会的，" 安东内利说。"明年，赛季的开始或中期，肯定会有机会。实现我父亲的这个梦想会很好。"
detailEn: Kimi Antonelli reveals plans to launch his own racing academy outside F1
F1 star Kimi Antonelli tells AMUS he wants to start his own driver academy and team up with his dad in a GT3 car
For Mercedes fans. All the latest from the Silver Arrows, with F1 news, driver updates, car development and race analysis from Brackley and Brixworth.

At just 20 years old, Andrea Kimi Antonelli is currently busy making the rest of the Formula 1 grid look like a bunch of sluggish retirees. But apparently, casually dominating the 2026 World Championship in a Mercedes isn't quite enough to keep the Italian phenom occupied.
In a recent sit-down with Germany's Auto Motor und Sport, Antonelli revealed that he is already plotting his next massive move outside the F1 paddock: building his own driver academy.

Following the recent paddock chatter around Lando Norris launching his own junior team, Antonelli wants a piece of the driver-development pie. And given that he literally grew up inside the garage of his father's GT racing team, AKM Motorsport, he knows exactly how brutal the financial ladder can be for a kid with talent but no cash.

"We want to build an academy for young people so they get a chance in motorsport," Antonelli told AMUS. "Motorsport is a great but difficult world. It is not easy to get opportunities there. We want to help young drivers get a chance."

Interestingly, Antonelli isn't focusing his future academy strictly on getting kids into the Formula 1 feeder series. He explicitly noted that professional GT racing is a highly viable, lucrative path - a mindset heavily fuelled by a certain three-time Dutch world champion.
Max Verstappen has essentially turned the GT3 endurance world into his own personal side quest, and the rest of the F1 grid is collectively catching FOMO. Antonelli is no exception.
Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing
"GT racing is growing strongly right now," Antonelli confirmed to AMUS. "Max is helping to make it more well-known and show the fascination."

With that booming popularity in mind, Antonelli wants his future academy to cast a wider net for young drivers. "That doesn't necessarily have to be in Formula 1," he added. "There are also many opportunities in professional GT racing."
Before Antonelli starts writing cheques for a full-blown junior academy, he has a much more personal piece of motorsport business to handle.

His father, Marco Antonelli, is a former touring car driver who built the highly successful AKM Motorsport outfit. While Kimi has previously tested his dad's GT3 machinery, the two have never actually shared a cockpit during a live race weekend. According to Kimi, that is about to change very soon.
Marco Antonelli, father of Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes

"We share almost everything, especially when it comes to motorsport. We also have joint projects for the future," Antonelli explained. "A dream of my father's is that we race together one day. I competed for his team three years ago, but we have never participated in a race together as team-mates. We would like to do that in a GT3 car."
When pressed by AMUS on a timeline for this highly anticipated father-son team-up, Antonelli didn't hesitate to put it on the immediate calendar.

"If we find the time, absolutely," Antonelli said. "Next year, at the beginning or middle of the season, there will definitely be an opportunity. It would be nice to fulfil this dream of my father's."

items.titleZh: 皮亚斯特里2026赛季正赛速度困境解析
items.summaryZh: 皮亚斯特里在2026赛季与诺里斯的正赛速度差距明显，奥斯汀站同策略下平均每圈慢半秒、最终落后22秒，他坦言目前还无法解释原因。
items.originalTitle: 'Superpower' neutered - Piastri’s fresh F1 struggles explained
items.summaryEn: Oscar Piastri is facing a clear race-pace deficit to Lando Norris in the 2026 season, averaging half a second per lap slower on the same strategy in Austin and finishing 22 seconds behind, and he admits he cannot yet explain why.
detailZh: 奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里在2026赛季的迈凯伦赛车上正经历与队友兰多·诺里斯相比的新困难，其中包括一个让车队领队安德烈亚·斯特拉所称的他的“超能力”失效的周末。
排位赛中诺里斯占据上风，以16比8领先皮亚斯特里，但两人之间的实际平均差距仅为0.040秒。
更明显的差距出现在不少大奖赛中，包括奥斯汀站。同策略下，皮亚斯特里（绿线）在正赛中平均每圈比诺里斯（橙线）慢半秒，最终落后22秒。此前还有巴塞罗那站（落后35秒）和赞德沃特站（落后32秒）这样差距巨大的周末，他承认“现在有太多比赛差距真的很大”。
被问及正赛速度的问题所在时，皮亚斯特里回答：“很慢。目前我没有更多可说的。”
“当伊萨克·哈贾尔从维修区出来时，看起来他遇到了某种问题，他的能量部署有点混乱。所以我在一些尴尬的位置追近了他，在那里损失了不少时间。
“从那之后，我在比赛剩余时间里基本上都在防守乔治·拉塞尔。但我觉得除此之外，速度显然不够好。所以有很多东西需要去弄明白。”
这对皮亚斯特里来说是一个挣扎的周末，因为虽然纸面上他在排位赛中击败了诺里斯——而且皮亚斯特里确实值得一些肯定，因为他做出了一个更快的合法圈——但他实际上比诺里斯最快的（因超出赛道限制被删除的）第三节排位赛圈速慢了0.424秒。
到周六时，皮亚斯特里的速度劣势已经非常明显，以至于迈凯伦在赛前会议上已经考虑到了可能需要交换两辆车的顺序，因为——正如车队领队斯特拉所说——“我们在周末期间看到兰多比奥斯卡稍快一些”。
皮亚斯特里在周五称奥斯汀站“从第一圈起就很艰难”，并补充道：“仅仅想让赛车发挥出性能就已经非常、非常具有挑战性了。”
“在排位赛的某些阶段，至少对兰多来说，赛车看起来是有潜力的，我觉得我们俩都感觉它确实有潜力。但能否把这份潜力挖掘出来，差距大概有半秒之多。”
“要从这辆赛车里榨出那个圈速真的非常、非常困难。我完全没能做到，但我觉得当我们俩中任何一人真正去推到极限时，就没法把车留在赛道上了。这确实是非常具有挑战性的一站。”
2026年的迈凯伦赛车确实具有刀锋般的特性，但诺里斯今年无疑更好地应对了这些。
最明显的对比是迈凯伦在夏休期前后的强势表现，如果没有马德里那次时机不佳的虚拟安全车，诺里斯本可以赢下四场比赛中的三场，而皮亚斯特里甚至没有登上领奖台（自五月初迈阿密以来也再未登台）。布达佩斯是皮亚斯特里最好的机会——在套圈卡洛斯·塞恩斯时的不幸接触让他错失了机会——但即便在那里，他在速度上也明显落后诺里斯一步。
但皮亚斯特里和迈凯伦认为他在最近几轮取得了进步，迈凯伦F1首席执行官扎克·布朗在新加坡表示，他“喜欢我在奥斯卡身上看到的一切，他感觉自信多了，完全掌控局面”。
皮亚斯特里相信自己已经解决了赛季初的一些弱点——但新的问题正在出现，这意味着结果看起来是一样的。
“这远没有我想要的那么有竞争力，”皮亚斯特里在奥斯汀说。
在我原本以为会很挣扎的弯道，以及今年一直很吃力的那类弯道，这个周末其实相当不错，但更多只是关于如何把整圈的所有环节拼在一起。
这才是真正的挑战。我不觉得情况与赛季早些时候完全相同，但最终结果仍然一样。
有点遗憾，但我对此并不太失望，因为我觉得自己一直在努力的方面仍然在展现出进步。
“超能力”被废掉了？
皮亚斯特里去年在奥斯汀也确实表现挣扎，最终获得第五名，而诺里斯则领先超过20秒获得第二名。
因此，这条赛道对皮亚斯特里来说相对不利，正如斯特拉在赛后所指出的那样。
“这是一条兰多擅长的赛道，也是奥斯卡相对更挣扎的赛道之一，”斯特拉说道。
“所以今年，我认为对奥斯卡来说尤其棘手，因为奥斯卡的超能力是逐步建立。一旦他建立起参照点，他就能真正高效地一圈接一圈地推进。但在这里，每一圈都不同。所以这些条件对奥斯卡构成了挑战。
“实际上，这些正是兰多发挥自己超能力的条件，那就是对条件极具适应性，尤其是在赛车打滑的时候。”
正是这种困难，皮亚斯特里整个赛季都在努力克服。他在2025年初展现出的状态，今年对他来说几乎完全遥不可及。在奥斯汀，这是因为不断变化的条件，而在此之前，则是试图重复那种与2026款动力单元契合良好的驾驶输入。
“这辆车需要付出相当大的努力才能做出圈速，并且需要驾驶输入达到比去年高得多的强度，”斯特拉在新加坡解释道——当时人们还希望皮亚斯特里在2026年的挣扎已经过去。
“这是车手们花了一些时间才适应[的]——好吧，‘适应’这个词不对，应该是理解。这也是奥斯卡在某个阶段几乎失去与兰多相比的部分竞争力的原因之一。
奥斯卡只需要明白如何迫使赛车做出一些事情，并接受开得快不一定意味着开得干净。
相反，这大概是奥斯卡的标志性特点，过去我们看到他快的时候，他开得很干净，那是非常好的数据，非常可重复，而且他很快。
“用这辆车，所有这些事情加在一起，似乎并不经常同时发生，所以对车手来说工作量很大。”
皮亚斯特里不得不适应，因为迈凯伦带来的升级都没有让赛车的最佳工作窗口变得更宽。
皮亚斯特里表示：“这些升级实际上都没有让赛车更容易驾驶，而这正是我们最大的问题。”
因此，本赛季这辆赛车不会变得适合皮亚斯特里，而且也不能保证迈凯伦能在2027年为赛车消除这种刀锋般的敏感特性。
车队希望拓宽性能窗口，让两位车手都能更容易地发挥出圈速，但归根结底，迈凯伦的首要任务是打造一辆快车。
而皮亚斯特里很可能要度过一个漫长的冬天，努力寻找答案，弄清楚如何在这些新规则下持续重新追平诺里斯。
detailEn: Oscar Piastri is experiencing new difficulties with the 2026 McLaren compared to team-mate Lando Norris, including a weekend that neutered what team boss Andrea Stella calls his ‘superpower’.
In qualifying, Norris has had the upper hand as he leads Piastri 16-8, but the actual average gap between them has only been 0.040s.

The more stark gap has been in a good number of grands prix, including Austin. Piastri (green line) is on average half a second slower than Norris (orange line), through the race on the same strategy, and ends up 22 seconds behind. This follows other weekends with big deficits like Barcelona (35 seconds) and Zandvoort (32 seconds), where he admitted there were “too many [races] now that have been really a long way off”.
Asked what the issue with his race pace was, Piastri replied: "It was slow. I don't have any more than that at the moment.

“When [Isack] Hadjar came out of the pits, it looked like he had some kind of issue and his deployment was a bit all over the place. So I was kind of catching him in awkward places and lost a fair bit of time there.
“Then I was kind of defending from George [Russell] for the rest of the race from that. But I think on top of that the pace just clearly wasn't very good. So plenty to try and understand.”

It was a weekend-long struggle for Piastri, as while on paper he outqualified Norris - and Piastri does deserve some credit for setting a faster legal lap - he was actually 0.424s behind Norris’s fastest (track limits-deleted) Q3 lap.

Piastri’s pace deficit was so clear by Saturday that McLaren had factored in the potential need to swap the cars' order in their pre-race meetings, because - as per team boss Stella - "we had seen during the weekend that Lando was a little bit faster than Oscar”.
Piastri called Austin “tough from lap one” on Friday, adding, "Just trying to get performance out of the car has been very, very challenging.

“At points in qualifying, for Lando at least, it looked like there was potential in it and I think we both felt there is potential in it. But the difference of extracting that potential or not is like half a second different.

"It's been very, very tough to get that laptime out of the car. I've not managed it at all, but I think when either of us have really pushed the boundaries, we can't keep it on the track. It's been a very challenging one, for sure.”
The 2026 McLaren does have knife-edge qualities, but Norris has undoubtedly dealt with those better this year.

The clearest contrast was McLaren’s purple patch either side of the summer break, where Norris would have won three out of four races without a poorly timed virtual safety car in Madrid, while Piastri didn’t even feature on the podium (and hasn’t since Miami in early May). Budapest was Piastri’s best chance - unfortunate contact while lapping Carlos Sainz robbed him of it - but even there, he was a clear step behind Norris on pace.

But Piastri and McLaren feel he’s made progress in recent rounds, with McLaren F1 CEO Zak Brown saying in Singapore that he was “liking everything I see out of Oscar, he's feeling much more confident, on top of things”.
Piastri believes he has fixed some of his weaknesses from earlier in the season - but new ones are appearing, meaning the outcome looks the same.
“It’s not been anywhere near as competitive as what I wanted it to be,” Piastri said in Austin.

“In the corners that I thought would be a struggle and the types of corners that have been a struggle this year, it's been pretty good this weekend, but it's more just been about trying to get everything in the lap together.
"That's been the real challenge. I don't think it's quite the same picture as what it has been earlier in the season, but the end result is still the same.
“It's a bit of a shame, but I'm not too disappointed in that because I feel like the areas I've been working on are still showing progress.”
'Superpower' neutered?
Piastri did also struggle at Austin last year, finishing fifth while Norris was over 20 seconds up the road in second.
So there is an element of this being a less favourable track for Piastri, as Stella pointed out after the race.
"This is a track in which Lando excels, and is one of the tracks in which Oscar instead struggles a little bit more,” Stella said.

"So this year, I think in particular for Oscar, it's tricky because Oscar's superpower is to build. Once he creates references, he can really effectively build lap after lap. But here, every lap is different. So these are the conditions that challenge Oscar.
“Actually, [these] are the conditions where Lando uses his own superpower, which is being very adaptive to the conditions, especially as the car slides.”

It’s that difficulty that Piastri has been fighting to overcome all season. His early-2025 form has looked almost completely inaccessible to him this year. At Austin it was because of the changing conditions, whereas previously it’s been trying to repeat the kind of driving inputs that mesh well with the 2026 power units.

“The car needs quite a lot of effort to deliver laptime and it requires a level of intensity in the driving input which is much superior to last year,” Stella explained in Singapore - when there were hopes Piastri’s 2026 struggles were behind him.

"This is something that took some time for the drivers to get comfortable [with] - well, 'comfortable' is wrong, but to understand. And it's also one of the reasons why Oscar, at some stage, he almost lost some of the competitiveness compared to Lando.
"Oscar just needed to understand how to force the car to do some things and [accept] the fact that driving fast will not necessarily mean driving clean.
“Instead, probably the signature of Oscar, when we have seen him fast in the past, [is] he was clean, it was really good data to see, it was very repeatable and he was fast.
"With this car, all these things together, they don't seem to happen very often, so it's a lot of work for the drivers.”
Piastri’s had to adapt because none of the upgrades McLaren has brought has made the car’s optimal operating window any wider.
“None of these upgrades are really making the car easier to drive, which is kind of our biggest problem,” Piastri said.
So the car isn’t going to come to Piastri this season, and there’s no guarantee that McLaren will be able to eliminate this knife-edge trait from its car for 2027.
The team wants to open up the window of performance so the laptime can be more easily accessed by both drivers, but ultimately McLaren’s number one priority is making a fast car.
And Piastri is likely to have a long winter trying to find the answer to how to consistently get back on terms with Norris in these new regulations.

items.summaryZh: 克里斯蒂安·霍纳离开红牛车队后，由于获得了巨额赔偿金，他无需在赛道上寻找新角色。

items.originalTitle: Christian Horner admits he doesn't need F1 return after £67 million Red Bull payout
detailZh: 克里斯蒂安·霍纳承认，在获得6700万英镑的雷诺车队赔偿后，他不需要回到F1
克里斯蒂安·霍纳在一次揭露性的新采访中谈到了他在F1的未来以及他的6700万英镑的离职赔偿金
对于红牛车队的粉丝来说，关注红牛车队，了解F1新闻、车手更新、技术洞察和米尔顿凯恩斯的比赛分析
当一位高调的F1高管被解雇时，谣言机器立即转向他们下一个可能落脚的地方。但就克里斯蒂安·霍纳而言，他在2025年离开红牛车队时，得到了如此巨大的金降落伞，以至于完全改写了他的职业轨迹。
而不是急于在维修区争取一个新的角色，这位52岁的老将正在为自己的F1生涯结束后作为一位高度流动的自由球员的生活进行规划。在最近的一次澳大利亚60分钟的节目中，焦点从导致他下台的职场政治转向了对可能回归的经济分析。由于提前终止合同，他的银行账户得到了大幅增强，霍纳正从绝对有利的位置计算着他的下一步行动。
当红牛GmbH终止了他的雇佣关系时，霍纳的合同还有四年多。解约的财务损失最近被揭露。根据红牛技术有限公司2025年的财务报告，霍纳获得了一笔惊人的6700万英镑（约合8850万美元）的赔偿金，一些车队的消息人士估计，一旦解决了额外的合同费用，总金额可能接近1亿美元。
这样的财富水平从根本上改变了霍纳对下一步职业发展的看法。
霍纳在直播中解释说：“我认为这给了我时间上的奢侈，我处于一个不需要回到一级方程式的有利位置。我认为生活中最宝贵的东西就是时间。”
尽管霍纳在英格兰乡村庄园享受着宁静的生活，并且目前正为英国美洲杯帆船队提供咨询，但他迅速确认自己的竞技动力并未消退。
“我仍然是个速度狂热者，”霍纳承认。“所以无论是四轮、两轮、四条腿……用马。给我看看赛道。”
车库里普遍认为，霍纳作为传统、拿薪水的雇员的日子已经结束。在直播中，记者塔拉·布朗指出，尽管关于他回归一级方程式的传言仍在流传，但霍纳只有在“他拥有车队的一部分所有权”的情况下才会回来。
在红牛的20年统治期间，霍纳是车队成功的终极建筑师，但他从未拥有过运营的股份。现在，霍纳拥有九位数净财富，这种动态已经完全改变。
如果一个陷入困境的中场车队或即将到来的制造商想要利用霍纳的冠军级专业知识来重建其项目，它必须提供董事会席位，而不仅仅是维修区。购买车队的一小部分股份立刻将霍纳从一名可替换的员工提升为特许经营伙伴。
无论他决定花钱重返赛道，还是选择退休专注于自己的赛马，这位前红牛智囊已经确保任何未来的谈判都将完全按照他自己的条款进行。
detailEn: Christian Horner admits he doesn't need F1 return after £67 million Red Bull payout
Christian Horner addresses his future in Formula 1 and his £67million severance package in a revealing new interview
For Red Bull fans. Keeping watch on Red Bull Racing, with F1 news, driver updates, technical insight and race analysis from Milton Keynes.

When a high-profile Formula 1 executive is shown the door, the rumour mill immediately shifts to where they will land next. But in the case of Christian Horner, his departure from Red Bull Racing in 2025 came with a golden parachute so immense that it completely rewrote his career trajectory.

Rather than scrambling to secure a new role on the pitwall, the 52-year-old is navigating his post-F1 reality as a highly liquid free agent. During a recent feature on 60 Minutes Australia, the focus pivoted away from the corporate politics that caused his downfall and honed in on the pure economics of a potential comeback. With a bank account heavily reinforced by an early contract termination, Horner is calculating his next move from a position of absolute leverage.

When Red Bull GmbH terminated his employment, Horner still had over four years remaining on his contract. The financial toll of severing that agreement was recently laid bare. According to Red Bull Technology Limited's 2025 financial reports, Horner received a staggering payout of £67million (approximately $88.5million), with some paddock sources estimating the total package closer to $100million once additional contractual fees were settled.
That level of generational wealth has fundamentally shifted how Horner approaches his next career move.

"I think it gives you the luxury of time, that I'm in a privileged position that I don't need to go back to Formula 1," Horner explained during the broadcast. "The most precious thing I think in life is time."

Despite embracing a quieter life on his English country estate and currently consulting for the British America's Cup sailing team, Horner was quick to confirm that his competitive drive has not faded.
"I'm still a speed junkie," Horner admitted. "So whether it's on four wheels, two wheels, four legs... with horses. Show me the racing line."

The consensus within the paddock is that Horner’s days of being a traditional, salaried employee are over. During the broadcast, reporter Tara Brown noted that while rumours of a Formula 1 return continue to swirl, Horner will only come back "if he has some ownership of a team".

Throughout his 20-year reign at Red Bull, Horner was the ultimate architect of the team's success, yet he never possessed an equity stake in the operation. Now that Horner is armed with a nine-figure net worth, the dynamic has completely changed.

If a struggling midfield constructor or an incoming manufacturer wants to leverage Horner's championship-winning expertise to rebuild its programme, it will have to offer a seat at the boardroom table, not just the pitwall. Purchasing a minority stake in a team instantly elevates Horner from a disposable employee to a franchise partner.

Whether he decides to buy his way back onto the grid or stays in retirement focusing on his racehorses, the former Red Bull mastermind has ensured that any future negotiations will be conducted entirely on his own terms.
